Class Explain

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.StoryGraphTool
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.SimpleStoryGraphTool
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.Explain
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.Task
public class Explain extends SimpleStoryGraphTool
A story graph tool that generates explanations that will improve the author utility and that characters believe will improve their utility.

After running this tool, the graph will contain all author explanations (where the character is null) for plans that can improve the story's utility.

It will also contain all character explanations which these properties:

  • The plan is possible from the node the character believes the current state to be (even if the plan is not actually possible).
  • The plan will improve the character's utility.
  • If the plan has more than one action, then for all actions after the first action, the explanation's character will believe those actions are explained for all of their consenting characters

All explanations, for the author or characters, are minimal, meaning the explanation does not contain a strict subsequence of actions which also meets the requirements above and achieves the same or better utility.

Explanation generation can be limited to only plans up to a set length.

Note that the first action in an explanation's plan may not be explained for all (or even any) of its consenting characters. This models the idea that, in the moment, characters want actions to happen which can lead to improving their utility, but they will not anticipate future action that they don't believe will be taken.

For example, consider one character purchasing an item they want from a merchant who wants money. The merchant does not know that the character wants the item, so the merchant does not expect the character to consent to buying it, but the merchant will still be happy to consent to the buy action because they will get the money they want. However, the merchant will not form a multi-step plan (such as traveling to the character to sell the item) if they cannot anticipate that the character will buy it.

Author:
Stephen G. Ware
